hypothesis: At fixed length, plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) lose weight from about November to March/April (spawning) and regain it from May/June to November, and this cycle is caused wholly by spawning and the rebuilding of tissues and gonads. In the ICES North Sea IBTS, whose Q1 cruises run mid-January to early March (during and just after the North Sea plaice spawning season) and whose Q3 cruises run July to September (recovery), this predicts for MATURE plaice: (P1) the condition factor K = 100 W / L^3 declines with date within Q1; (P2) K rises with date within Q3; (P3) in Q1, spent fish have lower K than maturing or spawning fish of the same length. If spawning is the WHOLE cause, IMMATURE plaice should show (M) no comparable within-Q1 decline.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported). Using NS-IBTS CA records (individual weights, CANoAtLngt = 1, maturity staged, length 15-55 cm) joined to HH records for haul dates, with log10 K regressed on day-of-year with fixed effects for 1-cm length class and sex: (P1) the Q1 slope for mature fish is negative with 95% CI excluding 0 and implies a decline of at least 2% of K per 30 days; (P2) the Q3 slope for mature fish is positive with 95% CI excluding 0; (P3) in Q1, spent fish have mean log10 K at least log10(1.05) below maturing fish at the same length and sex (95% CI excluding 0); and (M) the within-Q1 decline per 30 days in immature fish is less than 50% of that in mature fish (point estimate), or is not distinguishable from 0 at the 95% level.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered (claim refuted). (P1) fails with the opposite sign (a significant within-Q1 increase in K for mature fish), OR (P1) holds in mature fish but immature fish show a within-Q1 decline per 30 days that is at least 80% of the mature decline with 95% CI excluding 0 (the seasonal cycle is not confined to spawners, so it is not caused wholly by spawning). Any other combination (e.g. the pattern holds but immature fish show 50-80% of the mature decline, or P2 or P3 fails while P1 and M hold) is 'mixed'. If fewer than 500 mature plaice with individual weight, maturity and haul date are available in Q1, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).
interpretation: Thompson's table is for 55-cm fish from the 1909 Plaice Report, month by month. DATRAS does not give monthly coverage of the North Sea (NS-IBTS samples only Q1 and Q3), so the test uses the within-quarter trends that Thompson's smoothed curve predicts (decline Jan->Mar of roughly 7% per month; rise Jul->Sep of roughly 3-4% per month) and the maturity-stage contrast that is the direct signature of his mechanism. The word 'wholly' is tested with immature fish as the control that the assessors proposed: immature plaice do not spawn, so under the claim they should not share the cycle. Feeding and temperature covary with season and would produce a cycle in immature fish too; that is exactly what would refute 'wholly'. Planned years 2015-2024 (10 years, Q1 and Q3). Maturity codes are mapped before the data are seen: immature = {1, 61, A, I}; maturing = {2, 62, B}; spawning = {3, 63, C}; spent = {4, 64, D}; resting/skipped = {5, 65, E}; other codes (-9, 66, 6, F) excluded; mature = maturing + spawning + spent + resting. Length: LngtCode '1' means LngtClass in cm; '.' or '0' means mm (divided by 10). Fish with |residual log10 K| > 0.3 from the length-class/sex means are dropped as recording errors (pre-registered cleaning). A single probe request (NS-IBTS 2019 Q1 CA, HTTP status and first record only, a herring) was made before this pre-registration to confirm that the web service is reachable; no plaice data were inspected.
